name: Thimble Hollow
era_and_technology: A small valley village of lamps, carts and hand tools, with no telephones or engines.
everyday_life: Bread is the village's whole economy, and applewood is rationed because the orchard is sick, so every market ends in an argument over fuel.
history: The village grew up around its oven, which was built before the first houses.

places.name: The bakery
places.description: A warm, low building at the village center with the oven at its heart.
places.effect: People linger and tell secrets they meant to keep.

places.name: The Millpond
places.description: A still pond at the edge of the village.
places.effect: Nobody ever raises their voice there.

objects.name: The Weather Oven
objects.description: A huge black brick oven in the bakery.
objects.significance: Whatever is baked in it settles the next three days of weather.

objects.name: Mother's Starter
objects.description: A two-hundred-year-old sourdough culture kept in a crock in the cellar.
objects.significance: Every loaf in the valley descends from it.

powers.name: The Parish Council
powers.nature: Five elders who set the dates of the village's festivals and fairs.
powers.hold: They can appoint or dismiss the baker.
powers.felt: Most people only meet them as notices nailed to the well.

rules.statement: The Weather Oven works only when fired with applewood.
rules.cost: Every winter the village rations the orchard to keep the oven fed.
rules.when_broken: If anyone fires it with other wood, the weather is said to turn.

terms.meaning: a weather forecast baked into bread
